content.text: {"quote_faithful": "yes", "verdict": "confirmed", "evidence_kind": "counterexample", "fatal": "yes", "explanation": "The induction's stated conclusion is about ALL finite transversals, but the step only proves the criterion for X meeting C, while invoking the induction hypothesis for F_c in full strength (X traverses F_c \u21d2 X \u2287 some D_{c,k}) even though X need not meet C\\{c}. The quoted passage is exactly where the text restricts to transversals meeting C, justified only by C \u2208 F at the top level; C\\{c} is not a member of F_c, so the restriction is not inherited. The objector's instance is decisive: F={{1,2},{2,3}}, C={1,2}\u2208F. For c=1, F_1={{2,3}}, C'={2}; the restricted criterion yields D_{1,\u00b7}={{2}}, missing the transversal {3}; for c=2, F_2=\u2205 gives {2}. Final list {{1,2},{2}} misses the genuine transversal {1,3}. Since the sets B_j (hence L) come solely from this lemma, the finiteness obligation is unproved.\n"}
